style: 3D cartoon, Pixar, dry deadpan satire, vertical 9:16, hard white rim on her muzzle and on flying paper
motion_rule: she never stops running; the camera tracks sideways, the lane tearing past, new shot size every beat; two named moves per beat, opposite directions; her muzzle two thirds of frame height; motion across frame only, never up or down
character: a wiry macaque in a grey waistcoat running in the crowd, two arms, muzzle and jaw clear
second_characters: ONE rat porter a shoulder from the lens, crossing frame every beat on the move
props: a carrying pole across her shoulders, ONE pale jute sack at each end, identical and plain; ONE fistful of iron weights; A SWARM of blank slips
prop_continuity: one sack per pole end all clip, never doubled; both opened by the same tug, the same slips from both
environment: a dense river of porters, hand carts and rolling barrels fills a narrow roofed lane and pours past her every beat, bodies a shoulder from the lens on both sides; wet grey stone, slate clothing, white noon

light_events.event: a white shaft from a roof gap rakes her muzzle at the lens
white noon flares behind her, every flying slip edge lit

audio.delivery: level pleased female voice, words bitten off, even 4.45 syllables/sec, beats filled edge to edge
audio.pronunciation: GIR-ki do-LOY, SLE-va dol-GI, SPRA-va i-po-TE-ka, tol-KAY-tes, ba-LANS so-SHOL-sya, PRO-sto o-BE-ikh sto-RON
audio.pacing: speech unbroken 0.00-7.20, first word at 0.00, no gaps; sound fills the track to 10.00
audio.lip_sync: jaw opens on every syllable, no voice over
audio.sfx: iron wheels on wet stone, lane roar, boots, paper storm to 10.00

timeline.a: 0.00-0.45 she hurls iron weights past the lens; 0.45-0.90 the rat runs right to left a shoulder away, clipping the frame edge
0.90-1.35 left shoulder out, the left sack swings across to the lens; 1.35-1.80 a barrel rolls between her legs and clips her shin, stream left to right
1.80-2.50 right shoulder out, the right sack swings across to the lens; 2.50-3.15 a cart wheel bumps her thigh, a nearer row of porters runs left to right
3.15-3.60 she elbows another pole aside without slowing; 3.60-4.05 a porter clouts her left sack with his pole end, it flies out and swings back
4.05-4.65 she dives body first at the lens, both sacks thrown forward level at the glass; 4.65-5.20 the crowd splits around her, brushing both sacks
5.20-6.20 on the run she yanks the left sack tie, blank slips jet out sideways into a porter's face; 6.20-7.20 the same tug on the right tie, the same slips, a cart kicks the fallen paper at the lens
7.20-7.60 she spins on her heel, pole and both emptying sacks sweeping across the frame; 7.60-8.00 an oncoming porter ducks under it
8.00-8.40 she drives straight at the lens, pole angled to camera; 8.40-8.80 two porters part at the glass, one clips her shoulder
8.80-9.40 she dives muzzle first onto the lens, hurling both sacks into it, slips lashing the frame, jaw open; 9.40-10.00 paper buries the nearest porter

must_appear: porters pouring past every beat; two plain sacks, no writing, one per pole end, both opened the same way, same slips; at 4.05 both level at the lens; all words spoken, last by 7.20; muzzle over a third of frame, jaw open on every syllable
negative_prompt: subtitles, watermark, writing, digits, letters, signs, letterbox, horizontal frame, static camera, still background, wide or distant hero, parked hero, hero sitting or perched, hero moving up or down, standing bystanders, slow motion, scales, hanging pans, chains, tree, branch, bough, market stall, closed jaw while speaking, hands grabbing or carrying the hero, extra limbs, third arm, multiple monkeys, duplicate props, floating objects
